= BITwiki Page Types: Emergent Knowledge Patterns =

'''Version:''' 3.1.0-consolidated  
'''Status:''' Evolving  
'''Epistemic Status:''' These patterns emerged from use. They are not rules.

----
== Etymology: The Shapes of Knowledge ==

''Type'' — from Greek ''typos'' (τύπος), meaning impression, figure, model. From ''typtein'', to strike, to beat. A type is not a rigid category but an impression—a pattern that has emerged from repeated use, a figure that has stabilized through practice.

''Entity'' — from Latin ''ens'', present participle of ''esse'', to be. That which has existence, that which stands out from the background of becoming. An entity is not a fixed thing but a temporary stabilization—a moment of clarity in the flow of process.

----
== Purpose: Why Types Matter ==

Page types provide orientation in the knowledge field. They are not constraints but invitations—patterns that have proven useful, structures that facilitate navigation and discovery.

Types enable:
* '''Recognition''': Identifying what kind of thing we are encountering
* '''Navigation''': Moving between related entities
* '''Query''': Finding entities that share characteristics
* '''Extension''': Creating new entities with known patterns

They do not limit what can exist. They mark what has already found form.

=== What Page Types Are

Page types are patterns that have stabilized through repeated use. They are not categories imposed from above but regularities discovered through practice.

Think of them as paths worn through a forest—not because someone planned them, but because many travelers found similar routes useful. The paths exist because people walk them. The types exist because editors use them.

=== Why This Matters

When we say "this is a Topic page" or "this is an Idea page," we are not applying a rigid classification. We are recognizing a pattern that has proven useful for organizing knowledge.

The patterns can change. New patterns emerge. Old patterns transform. This document describes what has stabilized, not what must be.

----
== Minimum Criteria for Page Types

Rather than fixed categories, BITwiki uses minimum criteria—characteristics that help recognize a pattern without constraining its expression.

=== 1. Topic

A Topic page anchors a broad subject area.

'''Definition:''' A subject domain or field of knowledge.

'''What it looks like:'''
* Systems Science
* Cybernetics
* Artificial Intelligence
* Epistemology

'''Characteristics:'''
* Broad conceptual area
* Contains multiple ideas and implementations
* Serves as organizational anchor
* Hierarchical structure

'''Minimum criteria:'''
* Covers a broad conceptual area
* Contains or connects to multiple sub-areas
* Serves as an entry point for exploration

'''Not required:'''
* Fixed hierarchy depth
* Specific number of subtopics
* Exclusive categorization

'''Properties:'''
* Name
* Description
* Parent topic
* Subtopics
* Related topics

'''SMW pattern:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Topic]]
[[Has subtopic::Subtopic]]
[[Has related topic::Related Topic]]
```

'''Examples:'''
* Systems Science
* Cybernetics
* Epistemology
* Artificial Intelligence

'''Usage:'''
* Use for broad subject areas
* Create hierarchical navigation
* Group related content

----
=== 2. Idea

An Idea page captures an abstract concept, theory, or mental construct.

'''Definition:''' An abstract concept, theory, or mental construct.

'''What it looks like:'''
* Feedback Loop
* Emergence
* Recursion
* Homeostasis

'''Characteristics:'''
* Abstract rather than concrete
* Can be implemented in multiple ways
* Subject to epistemic evaluation
* Originates from thinkers

'''Minimum criteria:'''
* Abstract rather than concrete
* Can be realized in multiple ways
* Has identifiable origin or development

'''Not required:'''
* Specific epistemic status
* Fixed number of implementations
* Single originator

'''Properties:'''
* Name
* Definition
* Originator
* Origin date
* Field
* Implementations
* Epistemic status

'''SMW pattern:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Has originator::Person]]
[[Has implementation::Implementation]]
[[Has epistemic status::Established]]
```

'''Examples:'''
* Feedback Loop
* Emergence
* Recursion
* Homeostasis

'''Usage:'''
* Use for abstract concepts
* Link to implementations
* Track epistemic status

----
=== 3. Implementation

An Implementation page documents a concrete realization of an idea.

'''Definition:''' A concrete realization of an idea.

'''What it looks like:'''
* Thermostat (implements feedback control)
* Neural Network (implements learning)
* Blockchain (implements distributed trust)
* PID Controller (implements proportional-integral-derivative feedback)

'''Characteristics:'''
* Physical or digital instantiation
* Specific rather than general
* Observable and measurable
* Performance can be evaluated

'''Minimum criteria:'''
* Concrete instantiation
* Can be observed or measured
* Connects to abstract idea(s)

'''Not required:'''
* Specific technology
* Fixed performance metrics
* Single implementing idea

'''Properties:'''
* Name
* Description
* Implements (idea)
* Technology
* Developer
* Release date
* Status
* Performance metrics

'''SMW pattern:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Implementation]]
[[Implements::Idea]]
[[Has performance metric::Metric]]
```

'''Examples:'''
* Thermostat (implements feedback)
* Neural Network (implements learning)
* Blockchain (implements distributed trust)

'''Usage:'''
* Use for concrete systems
* Link to ideas
* Track performance

----
=== 4. Project

A Project page documents an organized effort with defined goals and resources.

'''Definition:''' An organized effort with defined goals and resources.

'''Characteristics:'''
* Time-bounded
* Resource-constrained
* Goal-directed
* Measurable outcomes

'''Minimum criteria:'''
* Organized effort
* Defined goals
* Documented outcomes or progress

'''Not required:'''
* Fixed timeline
* Specific budget
* Exclusive categorization

'''Properties:'''
* Name
* Description
* Goal
* Lead
* Organization
* Timeline
* Status
* Budget
* Team size
* Outputs

'''SMW pattern:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Project]]
[[Has goal::Goal]]
[[Has timeline::Timeline]]
[[Has status::Active]]
```

'''Examples:'''
* BITwiki Development
* Human Genome Project
* Apollo Program

'''Usage:'''
* Use for organized efforts
* Track progress
* Document outcomes

----
=== 5. Protocol

A Protocol page documents a prescribed procedure or set of rules.

'''Definition:''' A prescribed procedure or set of rules.

'''Characteristics:'''
* Normative (prescriptive)
* Reproducible
* Evaluable against outcomes
* Step-by-step

'''Minimum criteria:'''
* Prescribed procedure
* Reproducible steps
* Evaluable outcomes

'''Not required:'''
* Fixed compliance rate
* Specific validation status
* Exclusive categorization

'''Properties:'''
* Name
* Description
* Steps
* Outcomes
* Compliance rate
* Validation status

'''SMW pattern:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Protocol]]
[[Has step::Step]]
[[Has outcome::Outcome]]
[[Has compliance rate::Rate]]
```

'''Examples:'''
* Scientific Method
* Validation Protocol
* Consensus Mechanism

'''Usage:'''
* Use for procedures
* Ensure reproducibility
* Track compliance

----
=== 6. Dataset

A Dataset page documents a structured collection of data.

'''Definition:''' A structured collection of data.

'''Characteristics:'''
* Structured format
* Queryable
* Versioned
* Reusable

'''Minimum criteria:'''
* Structured format
* Queryable
* Documented source

'''Not required:'''
* Fixed size
* Specific update frequency
* Exclusive license

'''Properties:'''
* Name
* Description
* Size
* Format
* Update frequency
* Source
* License

'''SMW pattern:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Dataset]]
[[Has size::Size]]
[[Has format::Format]]
[[Has update frequency::Frequency]]
```

'''Examples:'''
* GenBank
* Wikipedia Edit History
* Climate Data

'''Usage:'''
* Use for data collections
* Enable queries
* Track provenance

----
=== 7. Event

An Event page marks a specific occurrence in time.

'''Definition:''' A specific occurrence in time with documented impact or significance.

'''What it looks like:'''
* 1956 Dartmouth Workshop (AI named)
* 2008 Bitcoin Whitepaper
* 2020 GPT-3 Release

'''Characteristics:'''
* Specific time or time range
* Observable occurrence
* Documented impact or significance

'''Minimum criteria:'''
* Specific time or time range
* Observable occurrence
* Documented impact or significance

'''Not required:'''
* Precise date
* Single interpretation
* Fixed scope

'''Properties:'''
* Name
* Description
* Date
* Participants
* Outcome
* Significance

'''SMW pattern:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Event]]
[[Has date::YYYY-MM-DD]]
[[Has participant::Person or Organization]]
[[Has outcome::Result]]
```

'''Examples:'''
* 1956 Dartmouth Workshop (AI named)
* 2008 Bitcoin Whitepaper
* 2020 GPT-3 Release

'''Usage:'''
* Mark significant occurrences
* Track historical development
* Connect to outcomes

----
=== 8. Person

A Person page documents an individual who contributed to knowledge.

'''Definition:''' An individual who contributed to knowledge.

'''What it looks like:'''
* Norbert Wiener
* Ada Lovelace
* Satoshi Nakamoto

'''Characteristics:'''
* Identifiable individual
* Documented contributions
* Connection to knowledge domain

'''Minimum criteria:'''
* Identifiable individual
* Documented contributions
* Connection to knowledge domain

'''Not required:'''
* Biographical completeness
* Fixed notability threshold
* Exclusive categorization

'''Properties:'''
* Name
* Description
* Contributions
* Field
* Affiliations
* Timeline

'''SMW pattern:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Person]]
[[Has contribution::Idea or Implementation]]
[[Has field::Domain]]
```

'''Examples:'''
* Norbert Wiener
* Ada Lovelace
* Satoshi Nakamoto

'''Usage:'''
* Document contributors
* Track intellectual lineage
* Connect to ideas and implementations

----
== Patterns in Practice

These examples show how types function in actual pages:

=== Example 1: Systems Science (Topic)

```markdown
= Systems Science =

Systems Science studies complex systems—networks of interacting components that produce emergent behaviors.

[[Has entity type::Topic]]
[[Has subtopic::Cybernetics]]
[[Has subtopic::Systems Theory]]
[[Has related topic::Complexity Science]]
[[Has related topic::Network Theory]]

== Core Ideas ==
* [[Emergence]] — System properties not present in components
* [[Feedback]] — Circular causal loops
* [[Homeostasis]] — Self-regulating stability
```

This page functions as a Topic because it anchors a broad area and connects to sub-areas and related fields.

----
=== Example 2: Emergence (Idea)

```markdown
= Emergence =

Emergence occurs when system-level properties arise from component interactions—properties not predictable from components alone.

[[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Has originator::Multiple contributors]]
[[Has field::Systems Science]]
[[Has implementation::Ant Colony Behavior]]
[[Has implementation::Consciousness]]
[[Has epistemic status::Established]]

== Implementations ==
* [[Ant Colony Optimization]] — Algorithmic implementation
* [[Neural Networks]] — Learning emergence
* [[Traffic Patterns]] — Urban emergence
```

This page functions as an Idea because it captures an abstract concept with multiple realizations.

----
=== Example 3: Thermostat (Implementation)

```markdown
= Thermostat =

A thermostat implements feedback control—measuring temperature and adjusting heating/cooling to maintain setpoint.

[[Has entity type::Implementation]]
[[Implements::Feedback Loop]]
[[Implements::Homeostasis]]
[[Has technology::Temperature Sensor]]
[[Has technology::Control Circuit]]

== How It Works ==
1. Sensor measures current temperature
2. Controller compares to setpoint
3. Actuator adjusts heating/cooling
4. Loop repeats

== Performance ==
* Response time: varies by design
* Accuracy: depends on sensor precision
* Stability: determined by control algorithm
```

This page functions as an Implementation because it documents a concrete system realizing abstract ideas.

----
=== Example 4: 1956 Dartmouth Workshop (Event)

```markdown
= 1956 Dartmouth Workshop =

The workshop where the term "Artificial Intelligence" was coined and the field formally established.

[[Has entity type::Event]]
[[Has date::1956-08-31]]
[[Has participant::John McCarthy]]
[[Has participant::Marvin Minsky]]
[[Has participant::Claude Shannon]]
[[Has outcome::AI named as field]]
[[Has outcome::Summer research proposal]]
```

This page functions as an Event because it marks a specific occurrence with documented impact.

----
=== Example 5: Norbert Wiener (Person)

```markdown
= Norbert Wiener =

Mathematician and philosopher, founder of cybernetics.

[[Has entity type::Person]]
[[Has contribution::Cybernetics]]
[[Has contribution::Feedback Theory]]
[[Has field::Mathematics]]
[[Has field::Systems Science]]
[[Has implementation::Anti-aircraft predictor]]
```

This page functions as a Person because it documents an individual with contributions to knowledge.

----
== When Types Overlap

Pages often fit multiple patterns. A person may also be an event (first to achieve something). An idea may also be an implementation (self-executing concept).

This is not a problem. Types are not exclusive categories. They are recognition patterns—tools for navigation, not constraints on content.

=== Example: Bitcoin

Bitcoin functions as:
* '''Idea''': Decentralized trust without central authority
* '''Implementation''': The actual running network
* '''Event''': Whitepaper publication, genesis block
* '''Topic''': Cryptocurrency, distributed systems

Multiple types apply. Use what serves the knowledge.

----
== Creating New Types

New patterns emerge when existing types prove insufficient.

'''Process:'''
# Document the pattern in use (3+ examples)
# Define minimum criteria
# Create SMW template
# Propose in discussion
# Iterate based on feedback

'''Criteria for new types:'''
* Serves a distinct navigational need
* Has multiple existing examples
* Cannot be adequately served by existing types

Types are not created by decree. They are recognized through use.

----
== Type Relationships: Webs of Connection ==

=== Hierarchical ===

```
Topic
└── Idea
    └── Implementation
        └── Project
            └── Dataset
```

=== Cross-Type ===

| From | Relationship | To |
|------|--------------|-----|
| Idea | implemented by | Implementation |
| Project | investigates | Idea |
| Protocol | governs | Project |
| Dataset | supports | Idea |
| Person | originates | Idea |
| Event | marks | Implementation |
| Event | involves | Person |

----
== Canonical Type Definitions ==

These types have achieved stability through extensive use. They are not exhaustive; new types may emerge, and existing types may transform.

=== Topic ===

Characteristics:
* Broad conceptual area
* Contains multiple ideas and implementations
* Serves as organizational anchor
* Hierarchical structure

Properties:
* Name
* Description
* Parent topic
* Subtopics
* Related topics

SMW:
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Topic]]
[[Has subtopic::Subtopic]]
[[Has related topic::Related Topic]]
```

Examples:
* Systems Science
* Cybernetics
* Epistemology
* Artificial Intelligence

Usage:
* Use for broad subject areas
* Create hierarchical navigation
* Group related content

=== Idea ===

Definition: An abstract concept, theory, or mental construct.

Characteristics:
* Abstract rather than concrete
* Can be implemented in multiple ways
* Subject to epistemic evaluation
* Originates from thinkers

* Name
* Definition
* Originator
* Origin date
* Field
* Implementations
* Epistemic status

SMW:
```wiki

[[Has originator::Person]]
[[Has implementation::Implementation]]
[[Has epistemic status::Established]]
```

* Feedback Loop

* Homeostasis

* Track epistemic status

=== Implementation ===

Definition: A concrete realization of an idea.

Characteristics:
* Physical or digital instantiation
* Specific rather than general
* Observable and measurable
* Performance can be evaluated

* Name

* Implements (idea)
* Technology
* Developer
* Release date

* Performance metrics

SMW:
```wiki

[[Implements::Idea]]
[[Has performance metric::Metric]]
```

Examples:

* Blockchain (implements distributed trust)

Usage:
* Use for concrete systems
* Link to ideas
* Track performance

=== Project ===

Definition: An organized effort with defined goals and resources.

Characteristics:
* Time-bounded
* Resource-constrained
* Goal-directed
* Measurable outcomes

Properties:
* Name
* Description
* Goal
* Lead
* Organization
* Timeline
* Status
* Budget
* Team size
* Outputs

SMW:
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Project]]
[[Has goal::Goal]]
[[Has timeline::Timeline]]
[[Has status::Active]]
```

Examples:
* BITwiki Development
* Human Genome Project
* Apollo Program

Usage:
* Use for organized efforts

=== Protocol ===

Definition: A prescribed procedure or set of rules.

Characteristics:
* Normative (prescriptive)
* Reproducible
* Evaluable against outcomes
* Step-by-step

Properties:
* Name
* Description
* Steps
* Outcomes
* Compliance rate
* Validation status

SMW:
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Protocol]]
[[Has step::Step]]

```

Examples:

Usage:

=== Dataset ===

Definition: A structured collection of data.

Characteristics:
* Structured format
* Queryable
* Versioned
* Reusable

Properties:
* Name
* Description
* Size
* Format
* Update frequency
* Source
* License

SMW:
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Dataset]]
[[Has size::Size]]
[[Has format::Format]]
[[Has update frequency::Frequency]]
```

Examples:
* GenBank
* Wikipedia Edit History
* Climate Data

Usage:
* Use for data collections
* Enable queries
* Track provenance

== Type Selection: Guidelines, Not Rules ==

=== When to Use Each Type ===

'''Topic:'''
* Organizing broad subject areas
* Creating navigation hierarchies
* Grouping related content

'''Idea:'''
* Describing abstract concepts
* Theorizing about mechanisms
* Connecting theory to practice

'''Implementation:'''
* Describing concrete systems
* Evaluating performance
* Linking theory to application

'''Project:'''
* Tracking organized efforts
* Managing resources
* Documenting outcomes

'''Protocol:'''
* Prescribing procedures
* Ensuring reproducibility
* Standardizing practices

'''Dataset:'''
* Referencing data collections
* Enabling queries
* Supporting evidence

'''Event:'''
* Marking specific occurrences
* Tracking historical development
* Connecting to outcomes

'''Person:'''
* Documenting contributors
* Tracking intellectual lineage
* Connecting to ideas and implementations

----
== SMW Implementation ==

=== Type Declaration ===

Every page should declare its type:

```wiki
[[Has entity type::Type]]
```

=== Type Queries ===

'''All Ideas:'''
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has entity type::Idea]]}}
```

'''Ideas with High Confidence:'''
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Has confidence score::>0.8]]
}}
```

'''Implementations of Idea:'''
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Implements::Feedback Loop]]}}
```

'''All Events:'''
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has entity type::Event]]
|?Has date
|sort=Has date
|order=descending}}
```

'''Contributions by Person:'''
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Has originator::Norbert Wiener]]}}
```

----
== Summary

Page types in BITwiki:
* '''Emerge from practice''', not imposed from above
* '''Use minimum criteria''', not fixed definitions
* '''Facilitate navigation''', not constrain content
* '''Evolve over time''', not fixed permanently
* '''Overlap freely''', not mutually exclusive

The types described here have proven useful. They are not the only possible types. They are invitations to pattern, not rules to follow.

== Etymology: The Shapes of Knowledge ==

''Type'' — from Greek ''typos'' (τύπος), meaning impression, figure, model. From ''typtein'', to strike, to beat. A type is not a rigid category but an impression—a pattern that has emerged from repeated use, a figure that has stabilized through practice.

''Entity'' — from Latin ''ens'', present participle of ''esse'', to be. That which has existence, that which stands out from the background of becoming. An entity is not a fixed thing but a temporary stabilization—a moment of clarity in the flow of process.

----
== Purpose: Why Types Matter ==

Page types provide orientation in the knowledge field. They are not constraints but invitations—patterns that have proven useful, structures that facilitate navigation and discovery.

Types enable:
* '''Recognition''': Identifying what kind of thing we are encountering
* '''Navigation''': Moving between related entities
* '''Query''': Finding entities that share characteristics
* '''Extension''': Creating new entities with known patterns

They do not limit what can exist. They mark what has already found form.

=== What Page Types Are

Page types are patterns that have stabilized through repeated use. They are not categories imposed from above but regularities discovered through practice.

Think of them as paths worn through a forest—not because someone planned them, but because many travelers found similar routes useful. The paths exist because people walk them. The types exist because editors use them.

When we say "this is a Topic page" or "this is an Idea page," we are not applying a rigid classification. We are recognizing a pattern that has proven useful for organizing knowledge.

The patterns can change. New patterns emerge. Old patterns transform. This document describes what has stabilized, not what must be.

This page functions as a Person because it documents an individual with contributions to knowledge.

----
== When Types Overlap

Pages often fit multiple patterns. A person may also be an event (first to achieve something). An idea may also be an implementation (self-executing concept).

This is not a problem. Types are not exclusive categories. They are recognition patterns—tools for navigation, not constraints on content.

=== Example: Bitcoin

Bitcoin functions as:
* '''Idea''': Decentralized trust without central authority
* '''Implementation''': The actual running network
* '''Event''': Whitepaper publication, genesis block
* '''Topic''': Cryptocurrency, distributed systems

Multiple types apply. Use what serves the knowledge.

----
== Creating New Types

New patterns emerge when existing types prove insufficient.

'''Process:'''
# Document the pattern in use (3+ examples)
# Define minimum criteria
# Create SMW template
# Propose in discussion
# Iterate based on feedback

'''Criteria for new types:'''
* Serves a distinct navigational need
* Has multiple existing examples
* Cannot be adequately served by existing types

Types are not created by decree. They are recognized through use.

== Canonical Type Definitions ==

These types have achieved stability through extensive use. They are not exhaustive; new types may emerge, and existing types may transform.

=== Topic ===

Definition: A subject domain or field of knowledge.

Characteristics:
* Broad conceptual area
* Contains multiple ideas and implementations
* Serves as organizational anchor
* Hierarchical structure

Properties:
* Name
* Description
* Parent topic
* Subtopics
* Related topics

SMW:
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Topic]]
[[Has subtopic::Subtopic]]
[[Has related topic::Related Topic]]
```

Examples:
* Systems Science
* Cybernetics
* Epistemology
* Artificial Intelligence

Usage:
* Use for broad subject areas
* Create hierarchical navigation
* Group related content

=== Idea ===

Definition: An abstract concept, theory, or mental construct.

Characteristics:
* Abstract rather than concrete
* Can be implemented in multiple ways
* Subject to epistemic evaluation
* Originates from thinkers

Properties:
* Name
* Definition
* Originator
* Origin date
* Field
* Implementations
* Epistemic status

SMW:
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Has originator::Person]]
[[Has implementation::Implementation]]
[[Has epistemic status::Established]]
```

Examples:
* Feedback Loop
* Emergence
* Recursion
* Homeostasis

Usage:
* Use for abstract concepts
* Link to implementations
* Track epistemic status

=== Implementation ===

Definition: A concrete realization of an idea.

Characteristics:
* Physical or digital instantiation
* Specific rather than general
* Observable and measurable
* Performance can be evaluated

Properties:
* Name
* Description
* Implements (idea)
* Technology
* Developer
* Release date
* Status
* Performance metrics

SMW:
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Implementation]]
[[Implements::Idea]]
[[Has performance metric::Metric]]
```

Examples:
* Thermostat (implements feedback)
* Neural Network (implements learning)
* Blockchain (implements distributed trust)

Usage:
* Use for concrete systems
* Link to ideas
* Track performance

=== Project ===

Definition: An organized effort with defined goals and resources.

Characteristics:
* Time-bounded
* Resource-constrained
* Goal-directed
* Measurable outcomes

Properties:
* Name
* Description
* Goal
* Lead
* Organization
* Timeline
* Status
* Budget
* Team size
* Outputs

SMW:
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Project]]
[[Has goal::Goal]]
[[Has timeline::Timeline]]
[[Has status::Active]]
```

Examples:
* BITwiki Development
* Human Genome Project
* Apollo Program

Usage:
* Use for organized efforts
* Track progress
* Document outcomes

=== Protocol ===

Definition: A prescribed procedure or set of rules.

Characteristics:
* Normative (prescriptive)
* Reproducible
* Evaluable against outcomes
* Step-by-step

Properties:
* Name
* Description
* Steps
* Outcomes
* Compliance rate
* Validation status

SMW:
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Protocol]]
[[Has step::Step]]
[[Has outcome::Outcome]]
[[Has compliance rate::Rate]]
```

Examples:
* Scientific Method
* Validation Protocol
* Consensus Mechanism

Usage:
* Use for procedures
* Ensure reproducibility
* Track compliance

=== Dataset ===

Definition: A structured collection of data.

Characteristics:
* Structured format
* Queryable
* Versioned
* Reusable

Properties:
* Name
* Description
* Size
* Format
* Update frequency
* Source
* License

SMW:
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Dataset]]
[[Has size::Size]]
[[Has format::Format]]
[[Has update frequency::Frequency]]
```

Examples:
* GenBank
* Wikipedia Edit History
* Climate Data

Usage:
* Use for data collections
* Enable queries
* Track provenance

== Type Selection: Guidelines, Not Rules ==

=== When to Use Each Type ===

'''Topic:'''
* Organizing broad subject areas
* Creating navigation hierarchies
* Grouping related content

'''Idea:'''
* Describing abstract concepts
* Theorizing about mechanisms
* Connecting theory to practice

'''Implementation:'''
* Describing concrete systems
* Evaluating performance
* Linking theory to application

'''Project:'''
* Tracking organized efforts
* Managing resources
* Documenting outcomes

'''Protocol:'''
* Prescribing procedures
* Ensuring reproducibility
* Standardizing practices

'''Dataset:'''
* Referencing data collections
* Enabling queries
* Supporting evidence

'''Event:'''
* Marking specific occurrences
* Tracking historical development
* Connecting to outcomes

'''Person:'''
* Documenting contributors
* Tracking intellectual lineage
* Connecting to ideas and implementations

== Summary

Page types in BITwiki:
* '''Emerge from practice''', not imposed from above
* '''Use minimum criteria''', not fixed definitions
* '''Facilitate navigation''', not constrain content
* '''Evolve over time''', not fixed permanently
* '''Overlap freely''', not mutually exclusive

The types described here have proven useful. They are not the only possible types. They are invitations to pattern, not rules to follow.
